Gordtopia · storage · read from 52 photos and 11 rollover videos, 6 September 2026

The Hold at the Bell

Fifty chests, one copper golem, nine words you already know. This is what you have, where it goes, and the six evenings that get you there.

Three passes. The chests were read slot by slot from your TV photos; the icons I got wrong were settled against the game's own textures and your corrections; the enchantments came from the rollover videos. Anything still marked (?) in the ledger is a best reading. The plan leans on the Copper Age mechanics, which are live in Bedrock 26.x.

What the chests say about how you play

The stacks said most of this. You corrected the rest, and the corrections are in.

Engines that are running

The mess, named

Sixteen of the fifty are dump chests: a bow, some sand, a diamond, a saddle, a potion, sixty four saplings. They are not the result of laziness. They are the result of having no rule for where a new thing goes, so at the end of every session the inventory goes into whichever chest is open.

Two other habits are quietly costing slots. Bulk and collection chests are mixed (sand lives in nine chests, saplings in five). And mob-drop floods are being kept as if they were keepsakes: 70 bows, 45 enchanted rods, 39 iron shovels, 25 tridents. That is 179 slots of things you will never wield, and four tridents and five rods you will.

The Bell: a large copper chest and a Quartermaster

The houses are for finding. The Bell is for filing. Inside the door stands one large copper chest. Drop your whole inventory in it and walk away. The copper golem takes up to 16 items at a time from the copper chest and carries them to a wooden chest that already holds that item, or to an empty one. It checks ten chests per search, reaches 32 blocks out, one block up and two down, and if nothing fits it waits seven seconds and tries again.

Two consequences shape the room. Every house chest must be seeded with its item before the golem can find it, which Evening 2 does by hand. And any empty chest inside the hall is a valid destination, so the only empties are the two overflow chests by the door, on purpose.

Bedrock does one thing better than Java here: its golem can tell potions and tipped arrows apart, so GATE can hold them in separate stacks.

Recipe: a copper block with a carved pumpkin on top. The block becomes the golem's copper chest. Right-click the golem with honeycomb so it never oxidizes into a statue. A second copper chest (4 copper ingots around a chest) placed beside the first makes the large chest.

Rule 1: the frame is the exemplar

One item frame on each double chest holding the one thing you would look for there. Not the category, the thing. A trident, not "sea stuff." You already do this on six chests.

Rule 2: the sign is the word

One oak sign per wall: the house word on line one, its noun on line two. HOLD / what shines. Nine signs, nine words, all of them already yours from the map.

Rule 3: if you do not know, it goes in the Bell

The only rule anyone has to remember. Nobody stands holding a thing wondering where it lives. The Quartermaster knows, and the overflow chests catch what it cannot place.

Six evenings

Each one fits a weekly session with James, Henry and Oscar, and each ends with something you can see. Evening 5 is the only one that leaves the hall.

  1. Evening 015 minutes, tonight, alone

    Walk the hall with this page open

    1. Stand in the glass hall and read the plan aloud once.
    2. Pick a wall for each house. HOLD gets the wall you see from the door.
    3. Count your item frames (you have about 10) and signs (2). Craft 12 more frames: 8 sticks and 1 leather each. You hold 23 leather and 47 sticks; cut one oak log for 16 more sticks.
    4. Craft 24 oak signs: 6 planks and a stick makes 3.

    Done when Every house has a wall and you can say the nine words from memory.

  2. Evening 160 minutes, with the boys

    Raise the Bell

    1. Break the three empty chests and the four near-empty ones. Empty chests are where a Quartermaster dumps strays, so the only empties left inside are the two you mean.
    2. Place one copper block just inside the door. Put a carved pumpkin on top. The block becomes a copper chest and the Quartermaster climbs out.
    3. Right-click it with honeycomb. A waxed golem never rusts into a statue. You have 10 honeycomb.
    4. Craft a second copper chest (4 copper ingots around a chest) and set it beside the first. That is the Bell: one large copper chest.
    5. Seed HOLD: move the vault chests to their wall. Drop 16 cobblestone into the Bell and watch where it goes.

    Done when The golem carries cobblestone from the Bell to DEEP without help. The boys have named it.

  3. Evening 275 minutes, the Council sorts

    Empty the dump chests

    1. There are sixteen mixed chests, two of them outdoors. Each brother takes three houses and works from the ledger: the ledger already sorted every stack on paper.
    2. Rule for the evening: a stack goes to its house, or into the Bell. Nobody stands holding a thing wondering.
    3. Consolidate on the way: sand lives in nine chests today and belongs in two. Saplings in five, belongs in one.
    4. Deepslate does not enter the hall. Carry those three chests to the mine entrance and call it the silo.

    Done when Zero mixed chests inside, and the two outdoor ones either emptied into the Bell or relabeled as outposts. Every double chest answers to one word.

  4. Evening 345 minutes, passive

    Cull the flood

    1. Craft a grindstone (2 sticks, 1 stone slab, 2 planks). Rods: keep the ones with Mending and Lure III, about five; grindstone the other forty. Bows: keep the enchanted ones and one plain bow for the Infinity book; grindstone the other sixty.
    2. Tridents: keep Impaling V with Loyalty III and Mending, Impaling IV with Loyalty III, Impaling III with Loyalty II, and one plain one for the Riptide III book. The other 21 are grindstone XP. Iron shovels and swords go in the blast furnace for nuggets.
    3. Smelt the gold, copper and iron armor you will never wear into nuggets in the blast furnace.
    4. Load both smokers with the raw chicken, beef and cod before you do anything else, and again on the way out.

    Done when BONES fits in two chests. The pantry smells of dinner.

  5. Evening 445 minutes, with the boys

    Sign the houses

    1. One item frame per double chest with its exemplar item. One sign per wall with the house word and its noun.
    2. Lay a one-block stripe of the house block in the floor in front of each wall: diamond block, cobbled deepslate, cyan glazed, white glazed, green glazed, oak planks, nether wart block, purple glazed, copper block. Every one is in stock.
    3. Photograph every wall. That is the new ledger, and next time it takes me ten minutes, not two hours.

    Done when A stranger could put a stack away in this hall without asking.

  6. Evening 5one whole evening

    The fortress run

    1. Fire resistance in the hotbar, 8 golden apples, a diamond kit, a bow with the 940 arrows, 2 lava buckets left home.
    2. Find a nether fortress. Blaze spawners are on the fortress bridges. Come home with 12 rods minimum.
    3. Brew: brewing stand (1 rod, 3 cobble). Eyes of ender: 12 (pearl + blaze powder). Ender chest: 8 obsidian and 1 eye.

    Done when An ender chest sits beside the Bell. Everything after this is a shulker box problem, and that is a good problem.

  7. Evening 645 minutes

    The Ford

    1. Three shelves by the door (stripped logs), powered by the two levers you own. A powered shelf swaps its three items with the right side of your hotbar in one click.
    2. Shelf 1, mining: pickaxe, torches, water bucket. Shelf 2, building: the palette block, scaffolding or ladders, a shovel. Shelf 3, the road: saddle, lead, bow.
    3. Put the FORD chest under them. That is the last thing you touch before any road.

    Done when You leave the hall in one click. All roads lead home, and now home has a door.

What this hold could enable

Sixteen things the numbers already pay for, with the arithmetic.

  • A full beacon pyramid, twice164 mineral blocks per max pyramid. You hold 933 iron blocks alone. Missing: the nether star.
  • The map wall at true extent77 tiles: 3,080 paper and 77 compasses. Compasses are 35 iron blocks. Paper is a sugar cane evening.
  • Full diamond kits for James, Henry and Oscar8 chestplates, 4 leggings, 5 boots, 3 helmets, 12 pickaxes, 7 swords. Exactly three helmets, so three full sets and not one spare helmet.
  • Twelve eyes of ender175 pearls is enough for 175 eyes; the portal needs 12 and the search eats a few. Missing: blaze powder.
  • A Quartermaster for every hallA copper golem is one copper block and one carved pumpkin. You have 1,768 copper blocks and 4 carved pumpkins.
  • A stained glass cathedral1,681 glass and all 16 dyes. Eight glass plus one dye makes eight stained glass. The hall already has a glass roof.
  • Anything a villager sells1,671 emeralds. Mending, Silk Touch, Fortune III, Unbreaking III from librarians; diamond gear from the smiths.
  • A Loyalty trident that comes back, and a Riptide one that fliesImpaling V, Loyalty III, Mending: throw it, it returns, every hit repairs it. And C16 holds a Riptide III book. Put it on a plain trident and you fly through rain and water. None carries Channeling, so mob heads wait on a librarian.
  • Wolf armor for a pack1,683 armadillo scutes at six a suit is 280 wolf armors, and scutes repair them too. The wolves of Wolfmark have never been safer.
  • A sculk XP farmThe single sculk catalyst spreads sculk when mobs die near it. Mined sculk gives XP. Place it where the fighting happens.
  • A rail line from the Bell to the mine1,180 rails is 1,180 blocks of track. With the 24 powered rails you have, about 900 of it runs at full speed. Craft 100 gold blocks into 600 more and the whole home country is on rails.
  • A Mending economy26 Mending books. Every diamond tool the boys carry can be made permanent for one book and an anvil. You will never mine another diamond pickaxe.
  • A glazed floor for the hall2,500 glazed terracotta in twelve colors. Five of the nine house stripes already use it, and that leaves about 2,300 blocks for the floor proper.
  • A trial chamber of your ownAbout 1,250 chiseled tuff and chiseled stone bricks is the palette of the place you took them from. Build the boys a vault room in the hall.
  • Flying machines84 slime blocks and 126 slimeballs. Two slime blocks, two pistons and two observers is a flying machine.
  • Copper armor for the whole Council12 copper helmets and 11 chestplates. Not strong, but every brother matched, and it oxidizes into character.

Critique, in three voices

I built the plan, then argued with it as the people who would argue with it.

The designer of Minecraft

in the design voice of Mojang, as I read it

  • You reached for the game's own grammar (frames, signs, a golem) instead of a redstone sorter you would never maintain. That is the intended play. The Copper Golem exists because most players never build the hopper machine.
  • Nine houses is a taxonomy, and a player mid-adventure does not think in taxonomies. She thinks "where does THIS go." The Bell answers that question so the houses never have to. Keep the page honest about which one is for filing and which is for finding.
  • The golem uses empty chests as a fallback. Your two overflow chests will fill with whatever is new. That is a feature. Empty them at the start of each session or they become the seventeenth dump chest.
  • Chest walls two high, never three. The golem reaches one block up and two down. A pretty three-high wall is a wall with a dead top row.
  • Wax the golem. An unwaxed golem oxidizes and becomes a statue. A statue is a lovely object and a terrible quartermaster.

An expert survival player

the voice of someone with a thousand hours

  • You are storing stone in a treasure hall. Deepslate is 137 slots and it belongs in a silo at the mine, not next to 4,000 diamonds.
  • Nothing in a mob-drop chest is worth a slot except the top three tridents and whatever has Mending. Bows and rods are grindstone XP. Iron shovels are nuggets.
  • Blaze rods are the whole story. Every real inventory fix in this game, the ender chest and the shulker box, is behind one fortress. Go this week while the fire resistance potions are still in date, which is forever.
  • You have 1,639 redstone blocks and zero hoppers. Five hoppers (25 iron) and six smokers turn the meat problem into a thing that happens while you build.
  • Give each boy a bundle. Leather and string are both in stock. A bundle is the difference between a full inventory and a full evening.
  • No compass in fifty chests, and a map wall on the Works Board. Thirty five iron blocks fixes it.

Gordon, simulated

a simulated voice from what I know of how you play; it is not your opinion

  • I do not want a warehouse. I want the hall to feel like the map does, and the nine words do that. HOLD, DEEP, STRAND. I already know them.
  • Do not make me stand at a smoker. Passive or not at all. If the boys want to build the hopper chain, that is their evening, not mine.
  • The Council ratifies numbers, not names. But they will want to name the golem, and a golem is a character, not a landmark. Let them.
  • The lore should ring at dusk. It should not read like a manifest with adjectives.
  • My life is not a sort key. If a rule wants me to move something that already fits, the rule is wrong. The tridents stay by the sea, not by the swords.

The lore

To be read at the Bell, at dusk, before Evening 1.

Every road in Gordtopia leads home, and home is a bell at 259 by 2466. For a long time the bell kept a secret. Behind it, under a roof of glass, stood fifty chests, and no one alive could say what was in them.

This is what was in them.

Four thousand two hundred diamonds, cut into blocks and stacked like firewood. Nearly eight and a half thousand iron ingots, every one of them mined by hand, pressed into nine hundred white blocks. Three thousand gold. Fourteen thousand redstone that has never been wired. And in one quiet double chest, one thousand six hundred and eighty three armadillo scutes, enough to armor every wolf that ever followed him home.

The sea had been here too. Twenty five tridents, won by hand in the water. Forty eight fishing rods glowing with enchantments. Nautilus shells from the drowned, and eight hundred blocks of chiseled tuff carried out of a trial chamber one stack at a time. Seventy bows and nine hundred arrows from every skeleton that ever aimed at the wrong person. Thirty nine iron shovels from zombies who dug their own graves.

And deeper things. Five ominous bottles taken from raid captains. A single chest of twenty six books, every one of them Mending. A single sculk catalyst, carried up from the southern bones at negative fifty, where the dark itself was still listening.

The three surveyors, James, Henry and Oscar, counted it all one evening and gave the hall its houses. The Hold, for what shines. The Deep, for stone. The Strand, for what the tide left. The Bones, for what the monsters dropped. The Rest, for food and growing things. The Mark, for maps, books and dyes. The Gate, for what came back through the Nether. The Reach, for the blocks a builder reaches for. And the Ford, for the road.

Then they built the Quartermaster. A block of copper, a carved pumpkin, and a dab of honeycomb so it would never rust. It stands by the door with one copper chest. Drop anything into that chest and walk away. The Quartermaster carries it, sixteen at a time, to the house that already holds its kind. It never gets tired, and it never gets it wrong.

There is one thing the Hold does not have, and it is the only thing that matters next. Not one blaze rod. No blaze rod, no brewing. No blaze rod, no eye of ender. No eye, no ender chest, no stronghold, no End, no shulker box. One fortress in the Red Country unlocks all of it.

The bell rings at dusk. Every road leads home. And now, at last, home knows what it holds.

Narration generated with a synthetic storyteller voice. About three minutes.

CORRECTIONS after full-res zoom
- C02 R1 col8 is 31 not 21: Diamond Block in C02 = 351. WORLD DIAMOND BLOCKS = 351 + 99 + 10 + 2 = 462 = 4,158 diamonds, plus 70 loose + 3 = ~4,231 diamonds
- C16 pink stacks = a raw meat, RAW PORKCHOP or RAW MUTTON by shape and hue, not rotten flesh. ~1,683 of it, never cooked. Gordon does not recall a pig farm; still open (see Corrections 2)
- C16 R4 dark block = SCULK CATALYST (deep dark / warden drop), not a shrieker
- Dark potions with red eyes = OMINOUS BOTTLE x5 (raid captains)
- Grey cup (x44, x31, x25, x21) = first read as buckets, then hoppers; Corrections 2 settles it as GUNPOWDER
- Red crumpled item (C08 x17, C48 x51) = first read as nether wart; Corrections 2 settles it as RAW COPPER
- Beige spiral with cyan = NAUTILUS SHELL (x3, x5, x2, x1 = ~11)
- Red-orange bar = COPPER INGOT (28 + 49 + 63 + 10 + 1 = ~151)
- Dark striated blocks in C38-C40 and C43 = DEEPSLATE, ~8,656 blocks
- Chiseled stone bricks confirmed by concentric-square pattern (also one of his item-frame labels)


CORRECTIONS 2, 2026-09-06 evening, after Gordon's replies, checked against Mojang's Bedrock textures
- Gordon: there is NO iron golem farm; he mined all the iron. The 933 iron blocks are pickaxe time.
- The red item x51 (C48), x59 (hotbar), and the small stacks in C08 are RAW COPPER, not nether wart.
- The grey cup item x44, x31, x25, x21 is GUNPOWDER (matches the pile texture; Gordon: "I definitely do not have 121 hoppers"). Inventory grey x64 is gunpowder too.
- C41 and C32: the green swirl blocks are CHISELED TUFF BRICKS (805) and the grey concentric-square blocks are CHISELED TUFF (386). Trial chambers, not an ocean monument. Gordon: "I don't have 805 prismarine."
- The pale yellow blocks read as sponge are sand or sandstone. No sponge, no monument.
- Arrows are arrows (not rails). Carrots x60 and x48 are plain carrots (not golden).
- The pink stacks in C16 are STILL OPEN: raw porkchop or raw mutton by shape and hue. Gordon does not recall farming pork. Hover to settle.
- Gordon has golden carrots, rails and minecarts that appear in none of the 48 frames, so the photo set is not the whole world.
- The pale speckled eggs read as turtle eggs are chicken eggs: Bedrock's cold chickens lay pale blue speckled eggs and warm chickens lay brown ones (Gordon: 'the eggs are bird eggs'). About 60 eggs of three kinds.
- Nether wart: the 34 in C33 stand ('a bit'). Leather armor is real and counted: about 13 helmets, 6 tunics, 3 leggings, 14 boots across C05, C08, C09, C13, C16, C17, C26, C29, C48.
- Bread: none confirmed. C33 R5c1, R5c4, R6c2, R6c3 are COOKED PORKCHOP (~224); C34 R2 cols 4-6 are BAKED POTATO (192). C33 R1c8 x53 is RAW CHICKEN, R2c2 x53 is COOKED CHICKEN. Gordon: 'I don't think I have 350 bread.' He was right.





How the read was done, and what I could not verify




Method
    

  • 48 HEIC photos pulled from chat 9 (four bursts, 15:52 to 15:57), converted, orientation normalized, the chest grid cropped at 1800 px and read row by row.
    • 

  • Icons I could not name from the grid were cropped again from the full 3024 by 4032 frame and read at four times the size. That pass changed nine identifications (sculk catalyst not shrieker, ominous bottles, nautilus shells, copper ingots, leather, deepslate, and the count on the first diamond stack: 31, not 21), and got two of them wrong, which the texture pass below caught.
    • 

  • Totals are sums of the readable stack numbers. Where a number was unreadable I wrote "?" and counted it as zero, so the totals are floors, not ceilings.
    • 

  • Second pass, after your corrections, against the game's own item and block textures pulled from Mojang's Bedrock sample pack, side by side with the crops. Changed: raw copper (not nether wart) on three stacks, gunpowder (not hoppers, not buckets) on four, chiseled tuff bricks and chiseled tuff (not prismarine and chiseled stone) on two chests, sand (not sponge). Confirmed: leather, arrows, plain carrots, diamond blocks, iron blocks. Then, on your bread question: the four tan stacks are cooked porkchop and the three golden ones are baked potato; the pale lumps are raw chicken, the orange ones cooked chicken; the pale speckled eggs are chicken eggs, not turtle eggs.
    • 

  • Third pass: eleven rollover videos, one frame per second, 250 frames, the tooltips read off 64 contact sheets. That is where the enchantments, the explorer maps, the wind charges and the two unphotographed chests came from.
    • 

  • Copper golem, copper chest and shelf mechanics checked against the Minecraft Wiki and two independent guides on 6 September 2026. Bedrock bucket stack size (16) checked the same way, which is what ruled out buckets.
    • 



Not verified
    

  • Which enchantments are on the 86 books outside C53 that were not hovered. The tridents, the rods and the diamond gear are now read from your rollovers.
    • 

  • The armor you are wearing. The chest screen hides the armor slots on Bedrock.
    • 

  • Whether any chest is still unread. The videos found two more (C53, C54) that no photo showed, so there may be others.
  • Two outdoor photos duplicated C46 and C48 and were matched by their contents, not counted again. The bursts also skip IMG numbers (3147 to 3149, 3161 to 3163, and others).
    • 

  • The hall's coordinates. One frame shows a readout fragment "486" and nothing else.
    • 

  • The pink meat in C16 (porkchop or mutton). Hover one stack.
    • 

  • Stack counts that were partly covered by the cursor or a durability bar. About a dozen, all small.
    •
